description: TITAN-1: 14,337 Parameters - Lightweight Space Image Restoration from Khulna, Bangladesh by Md. Akizul Islam. Tiny CNN autoencoder for edge computing. Evaluated on controlled synthetic benchmark (noisy-to-clean) to test feasibility for spacecraft computers. GitHub: mdakizulislam1-glitch/TITAN-1-BH-AI Demo: hf.co Apache2.0 CLPS Challenge
summary: TITAN-1 is a lightweight scientific image restoration engine with only 14,337 parameters. It recovers sharp details from blurred and noisy space images using a tiny CNN autoencoder built for spacecraft computers. Tested on controlled synthetic benchmark and SPHEREx-style sky survey images for Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It helps scientists see faint objects, comets, asteroids and possible new planets more clearly. Open-source, live demo on Hugging Face, reproducible on GitHub.
details:
TITAN-1 does: Input blurred/noisy image -> Tiny CNN autoencoder (14,337 parameters) -> Output clean, sharp image. How it works: Encoder compresses image, decoder restores details, trained on noisy-to-clean synthetic data. Benefits: Works on low-power spacecraft computers, fast, lightweight, open-source. Impact: Helps SPHEREx scientists find faint moving objects, comets, asteroids and Planet X candidates. Tools: Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Spaces, GitHub. Creative: Very small model, not large model, designed for edge computing in space. Tested with PSNR and SSIM, baseline comparison, limitations shown. ###

Live Gradio demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/mdakizulislam1/TITAN-1-Scientific-Image-Restoration - currently paused due to Hugging Face free CPU quota limit. Full code and Colab run instructions on GitHub: https://github.com/mdakizulislam1-glitch/TITAN-1-BH-AI - judges can run it locally.
